title: Adapting AI Weather Foundation Models to a Changing Climate
abstract: arXiv:2611.27605v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI weather foundation models learn from historical archives, while the climate distribution encountered during deployment continues to evolve. This growing model--climate mismatch motivates continual adaptation without repeated full-model retraining, but the structure of weather forecast errors determines how such adaptation should be performed. We develop an online adaptation framework that exploits two complementary error structures: geographically persistent biases and flow-dependent errors that vary with the atmospheric state. Analysis of Aurora-1.3B reveals strongly concentrated forecast-loss sensitivity in its decoder, motivating flow-dependent corrections within fixed low-dimensional sensitivity subspaces. A residual memory tracks persistent errors remaining after this correction, while a variable-wise online gate controls the contribution of the persistent component. We evaluate Aurora-1.3B using ERA5 from 1959--1968 for offline

translated_title: 将AI天气基础模型适配到变化中的气候
translated_abstract: AI天气基础模型从历史档案中学习，而部署时所遇到的气候分布却在持续演变。这种日益加剧的模型-气候失配促使人们进行持续适配而无需反复进行全模型重训练，但天气预报误差的结构决定了此类适配应如何执行。我们开发了一个在线适配框架，利用两种互补的误差结构：地理上持续存在的偏差以及随大气状态变化的流依赖误差。对Aurora-1.3B的分析表明，其预报损失敏感性强烈集中于解码器中，这促使我们在固定的低维敏感性子空间内进行流依赖校正。残差记忆用于跟踪该校正后仍然残留的持续性误差，而变量级在线门控则控制持续性分量的贡献。我们使用1959–1968年的ERA5数据对Aurora-1.3B进行离线评估。
tldr: 提出了一种在线适配框架，通过在低维敏感性子空间内进行流依赖校正并结合残差记忆追踪地理持续性偏差，使AI天气基础模型无需全模型重训练即可持续适应演变的气候分布。
en_tdlr: An online adaptation framework that combines flow-dependent corrections in fixed low-dimensional sensitivity subspaces with residual memory for persistent biases, enabling AI weather foundation models to continually adapt to a changing climate without full-model retraining.
